Quick update + initial findings (logs attached).

What I see: within the 07:00–07:40 UTC window there are repeated tenant-specific KV evictions correlated with a spike in prefetch worker backlog. Eviction pattern: multiple prefixes for `brightline-prod` were evicted within seconds, then aggressively re-prefetched, causing a tight loop. That behavior caused a hot key to saturate a small set of GPU workers; requests queued up behind a single hot shard leading to head-of-line blocking and batching lane starvation.

Evidence: attached `kv-eviction-log.txt` (snippet) and `prefetch-worker-stats.csv`.

Immediate mitigations applied at 08:27 PDT:
- Reduced prefetch concurrency for brightline-prod from 16 -> 4.
- Paused background prefetch for brightline-prod for 20 minutes.
- Increased tenant cache allocation by 15% via config (soft cap).
- Deployed a fallback routing rule: requests that hit a hot prefix are redirected to a model-variant with smaller KV footprint for this tenant.

Result: p99 dropped from 4.8s -> ~750ms within 8 minutes; error rate back to 0.2% and throughput returned to ~93% of baseline. We are still monitoring for recurrence.

Next steps (follow-up within 24h):
- Permanent change: adjust prefetch backoff logic to detect eviction loops and throttle auto-prefetch.
- Runbook update for tenant-level cache emergencies.
- Postmortem with RCA and customer impact numbers.

I'll keep logs rolling into the incident ticket.

-Grace O'Connor
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary for BrightLine incident (R-2026-3172) — decision requested

Team / Execs —

Summary: BrightLine experienced a p99 latency spike and elevated 5xxs this morning due to an eviction->re-prefetch loop for a hot prefix in the tenant's KV cache. The loop created repeated hot-shard saturation and head-of-line blocking that starved batching lanes on a small set of workers.

Impact: ~40 minutes of elevated tail latency (peak p99 4.8s), ~1.8% 5xx spike, throughput dip ~35%. Customer-facing downtime: degraded UX for search & suggestions.

Mitigation performed: reduced prefetch concurrency, paused background prefetch for the tenant, bumped soft cache allocation, and routed hot-prefix requests to a lower-footprint model-variant. Customer metrics returned close to baseline within 8–12 minutes post-mitigation.

Root cause (candidate): tenant workload with a small number of hot prefixes combined with aggressive prefetch settings and cache TTLs that allowed repeated eviction loops. Our prefetch/backoff logic did not detect the eviction loop quickly enough.

Recommendations / action items:
- Approve issuing a one-time service credit to BrightLine (proposed: 15% of March usage) — approval requested from Finance & Sales.
- Engineering: prioritize prefetch loop detection and automatic throttle (P1, 1 sprint).
- Product: add tenant-level prefetch override for enterprise customers (P2).
- Ops: add a runbook entry for immediate tenant cache isolation steps (pause prefetch, pin prefixes, increase soft cache).
- CS: coordinate customer comms + postmortem delivery timeline.

Please reply with approvals on the proposed credit and any other ask. I will schedule a short postmortem review tomorrow.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
